description: Add a durable local audit log of every system-of-record write (Jira-only today, schema extensible to Salesforce/HubSpot/Linear) plus four user-facing surfaces over it: per-meeting 'what this meeting wrote' trace, Settings â†’ Integrations status block, per-entity sync history side panel, and Inbox receipts feed. Plus an opt-in approval gate that lets cautious users require approval for low-confidence writes while keeping auto-push as the default.

userStories.title: SoRWriteLog foundation + Jira push instrumentation
userStories.description: As a user, every time Inwise writes to my Jira, I want a durable local record of exactly what happened so the rest of the transparency UI has data to render.
acceptanceCriteria: New NeDB collection sor-writes.db opened in main process. Schema: { id, targetSystem ('jira' for now, extensible enum), targetRecordId, targetRecordUrl, operation ('create'|'update'|'transition'|'comment'), fieldDiffs (array of {field, before, after}), commentBody?, sourceMeetingId?, sourceTranscriptSpan? ({start, end, snippet}), linkedTaskId?, confidence? (0..1), approvalPath ('auto'|'user'|'opt-in-gated'), result ('success'|'failed'|'pending-approval'|'retrying'), errorMessage?, createdAt, completedAt?, retryCount }

New module src/main/sor-write-log.ts exposes: recordWrite(entry) returning id, markCompleted(id, result, errorMessage?), incrementRetry(id), listRecent(limit, sinceMs?), listByMeeting(meetingId), listByTaskId(taskId), listByTargetRecord(system, recordId), aggregateByIntegration(sinceMs) returning [{system, total, success, failed, lastWriteAt?}]

Instrument every push function in src/main/jira-client.ts (createJiraIssue, updateJiraIssue, transitionJiraIssue, addJiraComment): wrap push body so recordWrite(...) is called with result:'pending' BEFORE the network call; on success markCompleted(id, 'success'); on failure markCompleted(id, 'failed', err.message)
For updateJiraIssue and transitionJiraIssue: compute fieldDiffs by reading current issue state via jiraFetch(GET) BEFORE the write so before/after is accurate (one extra GET per update; acceptable)
For createJiraIssue: fieldDiffs = the fields being created with before:null. For addJiraComment: commentBody = the comment text and fieldDiffs:[]
Update src/main/main.ts:390 (after-meeting auto-push) to pass sourceMeetingId, sourceTranscriptSpan, linkedTaskId, approvalPath:'auto' into push functions
Update src/main/main.ts:984 (on-task-update auto-sync) to pass linkedTaskId, approvalPath:'auto'. No meeting source
Push functions take an optional provenance parameter so future callers can supply or omit context cleanly
Add IPC handlers: sor:listRecent, sor:listByMeeting, sor:listByTaskId, sor:listByTargetRecord, sor:aggregateByIntegration, sor:retry (re-runs original push using stored params, increments retryCount)
Emit sor:write-completed IPC on every markCompleted so renderers can refresh live

On app startup, scan for entries stuck in 'pending-approval' or 'retrying' older than 24 hours; surface a one-time notification 'N Jira writes were interrupted. Open Settings â†’ Integrations to retry.'
Typecheck passes

Tests pass: unit tests for recordWrite â†’ markCompleted lifecycle; fieldDiffs computed correctly for update vs create vs comment; aggregate query returns correct totals; retry increments retryCount and re-runs
userStories.notes: Foundation story. All other stories depend on this. The fieldDiffs GET-before-write pattern is the only non-trivial design call â€” accept the extra HTTP cost in exchange for accurate diffs.

userStories.title: Per-meeting 'what this meeting wrote' trace
userStories.description: As a user, when a meeting wraps and Inwise pushes things to Jira, I want to immediately see what got pushed â€” both as a desktop notification and persistently on the meeting's detail view.
acceptanceCriteria: After the after-meeting auto-push pipeline (src/main/main.ts:390) completes, query sor-writes.db for entries with sourceMeetingId === thisMeeting.id

Desktop Notification (replaces the current generic auto-synced event): 'Meeting {title}: {N} updates pushed to Jira.' or '{N} pushed, {M} failed' if failures exist. Action button [See details] opens main window to the meeting detail view scrolled to the new section

In src/renderer/views/communications/TranscriptReviewModal.tsx (or the canonical post-meeting view â€” verify and use the right one), add a 'What this meeting wrote' section. Group by targetSystem (today: Jira only, but render the grouping)

Each row: operation badge (Created/Updated/Transitioned/Commented) + Jira key (clickable, opens targetRecordUrl via shell.openExternal) + one-line summary ('Status: Demo â†’ Proposal' for transition; '+2 fields' for update; 'Comment added' for comment; 'New issue created' for create)
Click a row to expand: full fieldDiffs table OR comment body; the source transcript snippet shown as a quote with timestamp
Failed writes shown with red badge + error message + [Retry] button (calls sor:retry)
Use existing tasks/communications styling â€” no new design system. Match JiraMappingModal.tsx patterns where applicable
If sor-writes.db returns zero entries for this meeting, the section is hidden â€” don't render an empty state
Listen for sor:write-completed IPC in renderer to refresh the section live (e.g., a retry succeeds while the user is looking at the meeting)
Typecheck passes

Browser-verify with dev-browser skill: simulate a meeting that produces 3 Jira pushes (2 success, 1 failure); confirm notification with correct counts; open meeting detail; confirm section renders 3 rows with correct grouping; expand a row; click a Jira key; click [Retry] on the failed one and confirm it re-runs
userStories.notes: The hero moment. This is the surface that lands the value prop visibly.

userStories.title: Settings â†’ Integrations status block
userStories.description: As a user, I want a small block in Settings that tells me at a glance: is each integration connected, when did it last write, how many writes this month, how many failed.
acceptanceCriteria: In src/renderer/Settings.tsx, add a new 'Integrations' section (or extend existing Jira section). Per-integration card:
Header: integration name + connection status pill (Connected / Disconnected / Auth expired)
Counts row (computed via sor:aggregateByIntegration for the last 30 days): '{success} writes Â· {failed} failed Â· last write {relative time}'. If no writes yet: 'No writes yet.'

Recent activity (collapsible, default collapsed): last 10 entries from sor:listRecent filtered to this integration. Same row format as US-002. Click â†’ opens the meeting detail (if sourceMeetingId present) or the SoR record
Action row: [Retry failed (N)] button (enabled only when N > 0) â€” bulk-retries all result:'failed' writes for this integration in the last 30 days. [Disconnect] button (existing functionality)
Today: only the Jira card renders. Layout reusable so future SoRs add a card without restructuring
Connection status comes from existing jira:status IPC. Counts come from sor:aggregateByIntegration({sinceMs: 30d ago})
Live-refresh: re-query on sor:write-completed IPC
No charts, no graphs, no per-day breakdowns â€” just numbers + recent-activity list
Typecheck passes

Browser-verify: connect Jira; confirm card shows 'Connected Â· No writes yet'; trigger a meeting with pushes; confirm counts update; force-fail one push (e.g., disconnect mid-write); confirm [Retry failed (1)] enables and works
userStories.notes: Trimmed from the originally-discussed 'integrations health dashboard' â€” solo OSS user does not need 30-day trend charts.

userStories.title: Per-entity sync history side panel
userStories.description: As a user, when I'm looking at a Task in Inwise that's linked to a Jira issue, I want to see the full timeline of what Inwise has written to that Jira issue, with field-level diffs.
acceptanceCriteria: In src/renderer/components/tasks/TaskDetailSidebar.tsx (verify path; this is the canonical task detail view), add a 'Sync history' panel below existing detail content
Header row: 'Synced to {Jira key} Â· last write {relative time} Â· {N} writes total' + clickable Jira key (opens targetRecordUrl)
Timeline: reverse-chronological list of all sor-writes.db entries where linkedTaskId === task.id. Same row format as US-002
Each row expandable to show full fieldDiffs / comment / source transcript snippet
Failed entries get the [Retry] button
Query via sor:listByTaskId. Paginate at 50 entries with a 'Show older' button if more exist (rare but possible)
If the task has no Jira link or no write history: minimal state 'No Jira sync yet. Auto-push runs when this task is updated or after the next meeting referencing it.'
Live-refresh on sor:write-completed if the entry's linkedTaskId matches the open task
Typecheck passes
Browser-verify: open a task that has Jira writes; confirm timeline renders correctly; expand a row; click Jira key; trigger a new write while panel is open; confirm it appears live
userStories.notes: Lower-frequency but high-trust surface. Cheap to build once US-001 exists.

userStories.title: Inbox receipts feed
userStories.description: As a user, when I open my Inbox, I want to see a passive feed of recent SoR writes so I can scan 'what's been happening' without opening individual meetings or tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: Verify which file is the Inbox view today (likely a section in src/renderer/Communications.tsx or MyTasks.tsx, or to-be-built unified Inbox from 7-page unification). Use the canonical Inbox surface that exists today; if Inbox doesn't exist as a discrete page yet, add the receipts feed as a section in Communications.tsx and note this for future unification work
Add a 'Recent sync activity' section. Renders the last 25 entries from sor:listRecent({limit:25, sinceMs: 7d ago})
Row format mirrors US-002 / US-003: operation badge, target record, one-line summary, relative timestamp

Each row dismissible (small âœ• that hides it locally â€” track dismissed ids in NeDB key-value or in config.json as sor.dismissedReceiptIds:string[]; new writes that arrive after the dismissed-list timestamp re-appear naturally as a side effect of being newer)
'Clear all' button at the section header dismisses everything currently visible
Failed writes shown with [Retry] affordance
Live-refresh on sor:write-completed
Typecheck passes
Browser-verify: trigger several pushes; confirm receipts appear in Inbox; dismiss one; confirm it disappears; trigger a new push; confirm it shows; click 'Clear all' and confirm
userStories.notes: Passive feed. Read-only. Receipts only â€” not approvals (those are US-006).

userStories.title: Opt-in approval gate with confidence threshold
userStories.description: As a cautious user, I want to require my approval before low-confidence Jira writes happen, so I keep auto-push on for the obvious wins but get a chance to review the risky ones.
acceptanceCriteria: Add config in Settings â†’ Integrations Jira card: toggle 'Require my approval for low-confidence writes' (default: off); threshold slider (visible only when toggle is on) 'Approve writes when confidence is below ___%' (default 60). Stored in config.json as sor.jira.approvalThreshold (0..1)
Helper text under the toggle: 'When on, low-confidence writes wait in your Inbox for approval instead of pushing automatically.'

In after-meeting auto-push pipeline (src/main/main.ts:390): for each intended push, before calling the push function, check: if toggle is on AND confidence is available AND confidence < threshold, then DON'T call the push. Instead call recordWrite(...) with result:'pending-approval', approvalPath:'opt-in-gated', and stash the full push parameters in a new collection sor-pending-approvals.db keyed to the sor-writes.db entry id
Otherwise, push as today (auto path)

New IPCs: sor:listPendingApprovals (returns entries with result:'pending-approval' joined with stashed payloads); sor:approve(id) (looks up stashed payload, calls appropriate push function with approvalPath:'user' provenance, removes from sor-pending-approvals.db, updates original entry's result); sor:reject(id) (marks entry as result:'failed' with errorMessage:'User rejected', removes from pending)

New 'Pending approvals' section at top of Inbox (US-005), separate from receipts feed. One card per pending entry showing: target record + operation + proposed fieldDiffs or comment + source transcript snippet that triggered it + confidence value if available

Buttons per pending card: [Approve], [Edit & Approve], [Reject]. [Edit & Approve] opens an inline editor on the proposed fields/comment; on save, calls sor:approve with the edited payload (extends sor:approve to take optional override)

Confidence source: if existing extractor returns a confidence value, use it; if not, treat all writes as having confidence:undefined and NEVER gate them (toggle effectively does nothing until extractor produces confidence). Document this clearly in helper text: 'Approval gate requires the extractor to provide confidence scores. Currently active for: {list of operation types that have confidence; if none, "No operations support confidence yet â€” toggle has no effect."}'
Pending approvals never expire on their own (user must explicitly approve or reject); show 'Pending {N} days' in the row
Typecheck passes

Browser-verify: turn toggle on; set threshold to 50%; simulate a meeting that produces a push with confidence 0.4; confirm push does NOT go through and a pending entry appears in Inbox; click [Approve]; confirm push runs and entry moves to receipts; turn toggle off; simulate another low-confidence push; confirm it auto-pushes as before
userStories.notes: Last because it changes existing auto-push behavior. Opt-in only. If the existing extractor doesn't produce confidence, the toggle is harmless and waits for that capability.
